records.text: Consequently, the Company’s marine transportation business is directly affected by the volumes produced by the Company’s petroleum, petrochemical and refining customer base.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The net result was a decrease of 41 inland tank barges and approximately 1,210,000 barrels of capacity.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: The decreases for 2021 were primarily due to reduced term and spot pricing in the inland market when compared to 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Cash provided by operating activities in 2021 decreased primarily due to lower revenues and operating income in the marine transportation segment, partially offset by the receipt of a tax refund of $119,493,000, including accrued interest, for the Company's 2019 federal tax return.

records.title: FORM 10-K
records.text: Generally, increases in weight per shipment indicate higher demand for our customers’ products and overall increased economic activity.

records.title: FORM 10-K
records.text: Generally, freight is rated by a class system, which is established by the National Motor Freight Traffic Association, Inc. Light, bulky freight typically has a higher class and is priced at higher revenue per hundredweight than dense, heavy freight.

records.title: FORM 10-K
records.text: Our revenue growth reflects higher shipment volumes and further improvements in our yield, both of which were supported by the strength of the domestic economy.

records.title: FORM 10-K
records.text: We regularly upgrade our technological capabilities to improve our customer service and lower our operating costs.

records.title: FORM 10-K
records.text: The increase in our cash flows provided by operating activities during 2021 as compared to 2020 was impacted by an increase in our income before income taxes of $487.1 million, which was partially offset by an increase in income taxes paid of $86.3 million and fluctuations in certain working capital accounts.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Ocean Transportation revenue increased $1,278.9 million, or 69.0 percent, during the year ended December 31, 2021, compared with the year ended December 31, 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Ocean Transportation: The Company’s container volume in the Hawaii service in the fourth quarter 2021 was 10.4 percent higher year-over-year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: As of December 31, 2021, the Company had $642.0 million of unused capacity under the revolving credit facility, which matures on March 31, 2026.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Operating Costs and Expenses for the year ended December 31, 2021 increased $634.8 million, or 30.2 percent, compared to the prior year.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Logistics: In the fourth quarter 2021, operating income for the Company’s Logistics segment was $14.8 million, or $5.2 million higher compared to the level achieved in the fourth quarter 2020.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: When compared to 2019, our operating revenue decreased by 25.4%, primarily driven by a decrease in revenue passenger of 29.6%.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Air traffic liability increased by $496 million, or 44.2%, driven by improvements in demand as customers begin to gain confidence to travel and resumed booking travel further in advance.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •System capacity increased by 65.5% year-over-year and decreased by 15.2% compared to 2019.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: •Operating expense increased by 31.0% year-over-year to $6.1 billion.

records.title: 10-K
records.text: Cash provided by operating activities totaled approximately $1.6 billion in 2021.
